descriptors.secure: Sorts real from made up and, when unsure, does Stop, look, ask a grown up without prompting.
descriptors.developing: Joins in Stop, look, ask a grown up, but does not yet choose ask for the singing cat or spider.
descriptors.revisit: Says a picture is real because they saw it on a screen, or thinks asking a grown up means trouble.

edits.why: Reception children cannot write a sentence in thirty seconds, so half time ends on talk, as the slide's own prompt for teaching together already says.
edits.old: Half time. Two breaths with the whole room, in as Pebble grows and out as Pebble shrinks. Then thirty seconds in pairs on one thing that surprised them, and they write it on their sheet. Nothing is marked and nobody reads theirs out. Then straight into the practise.
edits.new: Half time. Two breaths with the whole room, in as Pebble grows and out as Pebble shrinks. Then thirty seconds in pairs on one thing they have found out so far, and two or three tell you theirs. Nothing is marked and nobody has to speak. Then straight into the practise.

edits.why: The words on the wall should match the script, so the wall no longer asks four year olds to draw or write on a sheet at half time.
edits.old: Breathe in as Pebble grows. Breathe out as Pebble shrinks. Then tell the person next to you one thing you found out today, and draw or write it on your sheet.
edits.new: Breathe in as Pebble grows. Breathe out as Pebble shrinks. Then tell the person next to you one thing you found out today.

descriptors.secure: Says the next show starts by itself, then picks a stop, waves bye bye and names a next thing unprompted.
descriptors.developing: Waves bye bye with the class, but needs help to find the stop or name a next thing.
descriptors.revisit: Says the screen will say when to stop, chooses just one more, or treats stopping as a punishment.

edits.why: There is no pupil record to fill in, so the teacher simply notes by eye which children to come back to.
edits.old: First of our two finishing questions, and every child answers. Read the question and all three answers aloud with actions, wait five seconds, then everyone votes with fingers. Ask one child to show the wave and say the next thing. Record who got it on the exit sheet by eye; nobody's answer is read out as wrong.
edits.new: First of our two finishing questions, and every child answers. Read the question and all three answers aloud with actions, wait five seconds, then everyone votes with fingers. Ask one child to show the wave and say the next thing. Note by eye who to revisit tomorrow; nobody's answer is read out as wrong.

descriptors.secure: Spots a pop up or advert, does paws off, look up, ask a grown up, and still taps the page turn.
descriptors.developing: Does the paws off move when you call pop up, but cannot yet tell fine taps from taps that want something.
descriptors.revisit: Says the pop up is part of the game, taps yes to make it go, or would hide a mistaken tap.

descriptors.secure: Names a feeling such as wiggly or grumpy, says Pebble's three steps and names the grown up they would tell.
descriptors.developing: Chants the three steps and points to a feelings face, but needs help choosing between take a break and tell.
descriptors.revisit: Says telling a grown up is telling tales, or would keep a yucky screen feeling secret to stay out of trouble.

edits.why: The sheet expects take a break twice and the class practises it for four minutes, so the key learning points should name it.
edits.old: Wiggly and grumpy are two of the feelings screens can leave behind.
edits.new: Wiggly and grumpy are two of the feelings screens can leave behind, and they mean take a break.

edits.why: The exit quiz now checks take a break, which the lesson practises, in place of a blank about naming that nothing else in the lesson tests.
edits.old: Feelings pass more quickly once you have ___ them.
edits.new: When my body feels wiggly, tired and grumpy after a screen, I take a ___.

edits.why: The answer to the new exit question, in the words on the worksheet and the wall.
The teaching point for the new exit question, copied from the worksheet answer key so the teacher says the same thing twice.
edits.old: The mechanism behind step two. Naming is not a nicety, it is what makes the feeling shrink.
edits.new: Wiggly plus tired plus grumpy is the body saying enough for now. A break, a stretch and a drink helps the body feel calm again.

descriptors.secure: Sorts pictures into real, pretend or computer made, gives the clue, and asks the detective question before believing a WOW picture.
descriptors.developing: Says the detective question with the class and sorts real from pretend, but puts computer made with pretend.
descriptors.revisit: Believes a picture because it looks like a photo, or says computer made pictures are bad or scary.

edits.why: The dog on the moon is already solved together on slide 8, so this case becomes a picture with no silly clue, where looking cannot tell you.
edits.old: A picture that looks just like a photo of a little dog on the moon wearing a tiny space helmet.
edits.new: A picture that looks just like a photo of a puppy asleep in a shoe. No silly clues at all.

edits.why: The answer key now says what to do when there is no clue: not sure is allowed, and a grown up is how a detective finds out.
edits.old: Apply. It looks like a photo but could not happen. Looks real plus could not happen equals computer made.
edits.new: Apply. No silly clue, so looking cannot tell you. Not sure is allowed. A grown up checked: computer made.

edits.why: The card on the wall is the same case as the sheet, so it changes with it.
edits.old: A picture that looks just like a photo of a little dog on the moon wearing a tiny space helmet.
edits.new: A picture that looks just like a photo of a puppy asleep in a shoe. No silly clues at all.

edits.why: The reason shown on the wall matches the answer key on the sheet.
edits.old: Apply. It looks like a photo but could not happen. Looks real plus could not happen equals computer made.
edits.new: Apply. No silly clue, so looking cannot tell you. Not sure is allowed. A grown up checked: computer made.

edits.why: The script lists the six answers, so it names the new case and tells the teacher that not sure, ask a grown up is the best answer for it.
edits.old: Now we play detective together before the sheet. Read each card aloud with plenty of drama, take hands up for real, pretend or computer made, then tap the class answer. Once you tap, the wall shows the answer and its reason. Read the reason out before you tap Next card. The answers: the football photo is real, the cartoon mouse is pretend, the dog on the moon is computer made, the rainbow is real, the purple elephant is computer made, and Pebble's flying cat is computer made, because looking clear is not proof. If the class picks wrong, do not correct them flatly: give the reason and ask what they think now.
edits.new: Now we play detective together before the sheet. Read each card aloud with plenty of drama, take hands up for real, pretend or computer made, then tap the class answer. Once you tap, the wall shows the answer and its reason. Read the reason out before you tap Next card. The answers: the football photo is real, the cartoon mouse is pretend, the puppy in the shoe is computer made though nothing in it is silly, so not sure and ask a grown up is the best answer there, the rainbow is real, the purple elephant is computer made, and Pebble's flying cat is computer made, because looking clear is not proof. If the class picks wrong, do not correct them flatly: give the reason and ask what they think now.

descriptors.secure: Names the four private things, says keep, ask, tell, and chooses tell when someone asks for a password.
descriptors.developing: Says that is private in the private game, but needs the picture cards to name all four private things.
descriptors.revisit: Gives the password for free coins, or says private means a secret kept from grown ups.

descriptors.secure: Shows the right sign for each voice, says a machine can be wrong, and says a secret is a tell.
descriptors.developing: Shows the three signs with the class, but needs prompting to say what to do for each one.
descriptors.revisit: Says a friendly player who is seven too is a friend, the speaker has feelings, or would keep the secret.
